notes: Hand verdicts on every finding the differ classifies `breaking`, written against the Stripe changelog for the span (2022-11-15, 2025-03-31.basil]. `compatlab score` refuses to publish a false-break rate while any breaking finding is unverdicted, so this file is a gate, not documentation. Three verdicts are allowed: `documented` (a published change explains the finding), `undocumented` (the difference is real and Stripe did not write it down, which is a finding in its own right), `false-break` (the lab is wrong). Entries match on rule, normalized locus, workflow, and endpoint; any field omitted matches anything. `reference` cites docs/ground-truth.md by release and entry number. Where the changelog describes a restructuring without enumerating the fields it displaces, the note says so: that mapping is inference, not a quotation.

verdicts.note: `automatic_async` becomes the default capture method when the request does not specify one. Quoted directly by the changelog entry.
`GET /v1/invoices/upcoming` removed; 404 pointing at `POST /v1/invoices/create_preview`. RC1-607 found the changelog understates it — both call shapes 404, not just the all-subscriptions form.
Partial capture no longer creates a Refund, so the refunds list for the intent is empty and its count is 0.
The same change seen as the collection itself: one Refund on A, none on basil.
The Charge's own view of the same change: 3,000 cents refunded on A, 0 on basil, with no schema difference between them.

Invoices support multiple partial payments, so the single-payment fields were removed in favor of the payments collection. The changelog entry announces the capability; it does not list the fields it displaces. Mapping by inference.
Same restructuring as `charge`. Mapping by inference.
A boolean cannot express a partially paid invoice; `status` and the payments collection replace it. Mapping by inference.
